name: Völkisch movement
summary: The völkisch movement was a German ethno-nationalist current from the late 19th century to 1945 that saw the German people as an organic body with a quasi-eternal essence, increasingly defined by race. It sought national rebirth on reconstructed Germanic traditions, idealised rural life and rejected industrial modernity, rationalism, liberal equality and parliamentary democracy, and from the 1900s it turned strongly antisemitic. Its political wing, the Pan-German League, also demanded expansion, settlement of conquered land and a strong authoritarian state.
scope: The mainstream of the movement from the 1890s to the Weimar Republic as seen in the Pan-German League under Heinrich Claß (Wenn ich der Kaiser wär, 1912), Chamberlain's Foundations of the Nineteenth Century and Langbehn's Rembrandt als Erzieher, with the DVFP of 1922-24. It excludes Nazism itself, ariosophic occultism in detail, and post-1945 neopagan survivals. Several adherents' economic and gender views are inferred, since sources address them little.

keyFigures.name: Heinrich Claß
keyFigures.role: President of the Pan-German League 1908-39 and author of the 1912 programme Wenn ich der Kaiser wär.

keyFigures.name: Houston Stewart Chamberlain
keyFigures.role: Author of The Foundations of the Nineteenth Century (1899), a founding text of racial völkisch thought.

keyFigures.name: Julius Langbehn
keyFigures.role: Author of Rembrandt als Erzieher (1890), an early anti-modern, aristocratic and agrarian cultural manifesto.

universal-healthcare.rationale: No source documents a health programme; inferred from the organic-Volk idea that the nation's members owe each other care, so mild support for state provision to Germans.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Claß complains that wage rises and price rises feed each other and that employers lack state protection; wage floors are not a völkisch demand, so mild opposition inferred.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Claß says the once-venerated free play of forces has a bad side that crushes the Mittelstand, so the movement distrusts laissez-faire while keeping private enterprise.

public-ownership.rationale: Claß defends big firms like Krupp as organic and wants only limits on large banks, not nationalisation; inferred mild opposition to public ownership of whole industries.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Claß treats property and education as the groups politically robbed by mass suffrage and attacks liberal tax agitation; inferred opposition to heavier taxes on the wealthy.

unions-good.rationale: Claß demands that socialist trade-union leaders be expelled from the Reich along with party officials and editors, treating the unions as vehicles of internationalist agitation.

property-fundamental.rationale: Claß lists property with Volkstum and monarchy as the shared foundations of national life that every citizen must accept.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Claß proposes capping the capital of large banks and suppressing department stores to protect the Mittelstand, though he defends productive big industry; so selective regulation is favoured.

cut-welfare.rationale: The sources document no welfare programme; adherents were split between Mittelstand self-help and Volk-solidarity, so no clear answer can be inferred.

worker-ownership.rationale: Claß defends owners and entrepreneurs against a Socialist-led workforce and treats Marxism as poison, so worker takeover of firms is rejected.

surveillance-ok.rationale: No source speaks to this; inferred from Claß's call to crush socialist agitation without sentimentality that security measures would be welcomed.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from the movement's anti-modern, moral-renewal outlook that permissiveness would be opposed.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Never addressed directly; the movement's own antisemitic polemic and its wish to silence the socialist press make legal limits on speech against minorities unwelcome to it.

strong-leader.rationale: Per the Wikipedia article the German Völkisch Freedom Party openly demanded a "völkisch dictatorship", and the movement hoped for a leader to cut through parliamentary deadlock.

state-harmful.rationale: Claß speaks of the state's vital nerve and will to power as something to be strengthened; the movement is statist and nationalist, not anti-state.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred from the League's militarism and the wish to arm the nation that tight limits on gun ownership would be disliked.

empower-police-military.rationale: Claß insists army and fleet are also weapons of attack, and the Pan-German League backed militarist policy.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not documented; inferred from the movement's cultural-renewal moralism that adherents would disapprove.

decide-locally.rationale: Claß and the League push a unified, expansive Reich; Heimat sentiment exists but the movement's organising principle is the nation-wide Volk, so mild disagreement.

rehabilitation.rationale: Claß calls for hard will and no sentimentality toward enemies of the nation; inferred preference for punishment over rehabilitation.

traditional-family.rationale: The movement idealised rural life and an authentic quasi-eternal Volk; the traditional family as its carrier is implied rather than set out in the sources opened.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the movement's rejection of modernity and its stress on biological reproduction of the Volk.

abortion-legal.rationale: Claß describes Germany's growing population as a source of strength and a reason for expansion, so inferred opposition to abortion rights.

more-religion-public.rationale: Adherents split between a Germanized Christianity and a revived Germanic paganism, and Claß blames materialism rather than secularism; no single answer.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Claß says the belief in human equality behind Jewish emancipation was a mistake and that race is the source of danger; remedial measures for racial groups would be rejected.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not discussed; the movement's essentialism about Volk and blood suggests it would regard sex differences as natural.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The Wikipedia article says the movement's common core was national rebirth through reconstructed ancient Germanic traditions and a Volk essence.

gradual-change.rationale: Völkisch groups sought a radical rebirth of the nation and a break with modernity, not gradual adaptation of existing institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Claß wants to block Jewish influence and restrict rights of the resident Jewish population, so inflows of foreigners are opposed.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Claß condemns internationalism as the Socialist-Jewish poison and wants loyalty to the Volk-state.

free-trade.rationale: Claß seeks colonies for raw materials and markets and attacks the free play of forces; inferred preference for protected, self-sufficient economy.

nation-first.rationale: Claß holds that Germany's interests and land hunger justify aggressive policy regardless of other states' wishes.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: No source addresses it; Claß's explicit contempt for sentimentality and for other states' preferences suggest rights-based intervention would not be a priority.

open-borders.rationale: The League wanted Germans protected from mixing with other races, and the movement defined the nation by blood.

limit-growth.rationale: Adherents idealised nature and rural life but Pan-Germans like Claß wanted industry and expansion; split.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed; nature romanticism and pro-industry nationalism pull in opposite directions.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The movement opposed industrialization, scientific rationalism and mass society, so technological salvation is rejected.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Nuclear power is anachronistic for the movement, and the sources give no principle (nature romanticism versus industrial self-sufficiency) that decides it.

revolution-justified.rationale: Claß plotted a coup in 1911 and again in 1926 to impose a plebiscitary or authoritarian order, so extra-legal change was acceptable to some adherents.

experts-over-public.rationale: Claß argues the worthy and capable should not be treated like the unfit masses; inferred tilt toward elite expertise over mass opinion.

central-planning.rationale: Claß defends private industrial leaders and organic enterprises; planned economy is a Socialist idea he rejects.

socialized-markets.rationale: Claß rejects the Socialist programme and defends owners; worker or public ownership is not part of the movement's economics.

land-value-tax.rationale: Land reform circles overlapped with the movement but no opened source documents a position.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Claß treats property and heritage as national foundations; inferred opposition to heavy inheritance taxes.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; unconditional state payments cut against the movement's emphasis on service to the nation and Claß's work ethic contrast.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Claß seeks economic independence through colonies and protection of the Mittelstand against big capital; protection is inferred as congenial.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Claß wants limits on banks and strong state backing for industry but defends private firms; adherents not clearly aligned.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Claß wants the Mittelstand protected against big capital and notes large estates can be split into smaller farms; Langbehn wanted an agrarian society.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Claß defends private property and enterprise and treats Marxist doctrine as poison, so abolishing money and wage labour is rejected.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Claß wants a cap on the capital of large banks, but no opened source discusses central banks or state money, so no direction can be inferred.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Inferred from the organic-Volk idea that estates should be organised as parts of one body rather than opposed classes.

one-party-rule.rationale: The DVFP demanded a völkisch dictatorship, implying rule by one movement, though völkisch groups were fractious.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Claß names monarchy among the foundations of national life, and Langbehn wanted a monarch, though Claß blamed the court for failing the nation.

democracy-best.rationale: Claß states that universal equal suffrage has always been an untruth, immoral because it treats the worthy like the unfit, and unjust because masses disenfranchise the educated and propertied.

direct-votes.rationale: Claß's objection to rule by mass votes makes broad direct lawmaking by citizens unwelcome, though a plebiscitary dictator was considered.

workers-councils.rationale: Councils of workers as the basis of power embody the Socialist programme that Claß wanted to ban and expel.

right-to-secede.rationale: The League's imperial nationalism and demand for unconditional submission to the national whole exclude secession.

natural-rulers.rationale: Claß says it is wrong to treat the worthy, capable and mature the same as the unworthy, unfit and immature, and Langbehn held that equality is death.

political-violence-never.rationale: Claß calls for hard will without sentimentality, mass expulsions of socialist leaders and aggressive war; violence in politics is accepted.

war-builds-character.rationale: Social Darwinism was strong in the League and Claß urged army and fleet as weapons of attack; Langbehn is an exception who favoured peace.

separate-church-state.rationale: Adherents wanted Christianity Germanized or replaced by a Germanic faith, so national and religious life were meant to merge.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Law was meant to follow the Volk's blood and tradition, not a revealed text; pagan strands would reject scripture outright.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Claß treats the state's will to power as vital and defence as the nation's job.

military-superiority.rationale: Claß wants Germany to stop being satiated and to expand, backed by army and fleet.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The Wikipedia article calls the movement a Pan-German ethno-nationalist current whose Volk idea shifted into a racial essence.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Claß identifies race, not class, as the source of danger and calls the Socialist agitation poison among the masses.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Claß says the idea of human equality was never realisable and that the equal vote is untrue and unjust.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Pan-German settlement plans treat conquered land as German settlement territory, not under native authority.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Claß demands more colonial land and says other states' feelings do not matter.

civilizational-union.rationale: Pan-Germanism sought union by shared German ancestry; inferred approval of unions by shared stock, less by religion.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Claß contrasts the German who stands above possession and acts from honour with the Jew who subordinates everything to gain.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Claß and the League demand that the individual submit to the national whole and defend the state, putting obligation to the Volk ahead of personal claims.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Romanticism and an idealised rural life are part of the movement, but sources opened do not state nature's intrinsic worth.

limit-population.rationale: Claß treats rapid population growth as a reason for expansion and for settlement land, not a problem to be curbed.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The article says the movement opposed industrialization, urbanization and mass society; Pan-German leaders like Claß were more accepting of heavy industry.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The movement stressed rooted tradition and opposed modernity, so speeding disruptive change is rejected.

human-enhancement.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement's anti-modern spirit suggests distaste, though racial hygiene aimed at improving the stock.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the movement's rejection of rationalist mass society and preference for personal leaders.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Claß's preference for a strong state that watches and expels its enemies that citizens' secrecy from the state would be disliked.

restore-past-order.rationale: The movement's core hope was national rebirth based on reconstructed ancient Germanic traditions and an idealised Holy Roman Empire.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The Weltanschauung of Volk and race was treated as primary, so judging by results alone would be disliked.

direct-action.rationale: Claß backed coup plans against parliament, so extra-parliamentary action was accepted by some.

means-match-ends.rationale: Claß urges harsh methods regardless of sentiment, implying means need not reflect the ideal.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The movement glorified agrarian peasants, not hunter-gatherers; it is unrelated but its glorified farming life points away from foraging.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Part of the Marxist programme that Claß wanted suppressed; the movement's estate and organic thinking assumes differentiated roles.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Claß rejects equality and the Socialist programme and celebrates differences of worth.

production-for-use.rationale: Claß defends private industrial enterprise and the entrepreneurs as pillars of the national economy.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Claß defends entrepreneurs against the workers and blames Jews, not owners, for exploiting Germans.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Claß wants Social Democracy broken by expelling its deputies, editors and union leaders, so rule of workers over other classes is the opposite of his programme.

collective-farming.rationale: The movement idealised the independent peasant on his own soil, so collectivised agriculture runs against its core agrarian ideal.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Claß attributes expansion to the state's will to power and national needs, not to capitalism.

taxation-theft.rationale: Claß treats the state as the nation's life and calls tax agitation by liberals suicidal; the notion of taxation as theft is alien.

harm-principle.rationale: Claß wants the state to strengthen national life and restrict Jews and Socialists on grounds of national danger, not just individual harm.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The Wikipedia article on the League says it demanded that individuals submit unconditionally to the national whole, represented by the state.

conscription.rationale: The League backed militarist policy and Claß treated the army as an instrument of attack and national greatness.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The national whole commands the individual, so a freedom to leave as the main check on government makes no sense to the movement.

state-as-business.rationale: Claß sees the state as a living will to power, with honour above gain, not a commercial service.

positive-liberty.rationale: Claß's Volk-first, anti-equality view does not recognise material entitlements to freedom.

media-academia-power.rationale: Claß claims Jews stand between rulers and people and that liberal and socialist presses undermine the nation.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The Wikipedia article on Chamberlain's Foundations says he held races differ in their gifts and placed Teutons at the top of the Aryan race.

organic-representation.rationale: Claß proposes a franchise reform favouring property and education and sees the nation as organic; estate-based representation is inferred as congenial.

total-state.rationale: The League demanded unconditional submission of individuals to the national whole, suggesting broad state direction, though the movement was not a state-planning ideology.

national-rebirth.rationale: The Wikipedia article states the common core of the movement was hope for national rebirth to overcome decadence through ancient Germanic traditions.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Claß says Germany has become hungry for land and that its territory does not meet the needs of the German people, whatever other states think.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Germanic Gefolgschaft was part of the idealised past and a leader principle appears later, so oaths of loyalty are inferred as favoured.

bound-labor.rationale: The movement idealised free peasants on the soil but not legal serfdom to a lord.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Völkisch thinkers held that knowledge was rooted in Volk and blood, but they did not frame it as reflecting power; inferred weak disagreement.

universal-morality.rationale: Claß states German and Jew differ at the deepest level like fire and water in their view of life, rejecting a shared human morality.

single-common-good.rationale: The organic Volk is one body with one essence, so a single common good is implied.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The movement denied Jews any claim to belong and Claß wanted their rights restricted; support for a Jewish state right is not documented and the stance was hostile.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Pan-Germanism sought to unite Germans beyond the Reich's borders, implying return and citizenship for ethnic Germans abroad.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language was a marker of the Volk and Germanic revival was central; inferred support.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Claß wants state protection for employers against workers, so worker votes in firms are rejected.

school-vouchers.rationale: No opened source touches school finance; adherents wanted national schooling, but a voucher scheme is not something they discussed.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is not addressed by the sources; Claß criticises tax agitation but says nothing on deficits.

economic-freedom.rationale: Claß says the free play of forces ruins the Mittelstand, so economic freedom is not a condition of political life.

rule-by-example.rationale: Claß's picture of the German as honour-driven and above possession suggests leaders should rule through character.

national-self-determination.rationale: The movement's ethnic nationalism implies a state for each Volk, but it also demanded dominion over Poles and Slavs.

force-without-un.rationale: Anachronistic; Claß explicitly wants an aggressive foreign policy regardless of others.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The article says the movement opposed scientific rationalism and exalted an intuitive Volk essence.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Inferred from the Volk-first principle that benefits belong to members of the nation.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Claß contrasts the German honour and effort ethos with the Jewish pursuit of gain; inferred approval of work requirements.

class-collaboration.rationale: Claß wants workers returned from Socialist leaders to national loyalty and employers protected, imagining one national community.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The movement revered inherited Germanic tradition and wanted to restore it.

dominated-front.rationale: Pan-German rivalry with Britain and France exists but a common front with non-Western peoples is not documented.

workers-nation.rationale: Claß treats the workers' defection from the fatherland as the danger and wants them returned to the nation.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Inferred from the movement's traditionalism and anti-modern stance; no opened source states it.

ban-interest.rationale: Völkisch circles denounced Jewish finance and Claß wanted big banks capped, but interest bans are not documented in opened sources.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Claß demands general restriction of the rights of resident Jews and says race is the source of danger.

state-class-instrument.rationale: For Claß the state is the nation's vital nerve and will to power, the organ of the whole Volk, not a tool of one class.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Anachronistic; Claß wants self-sufficiency in raw materials but no source addresses energy.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Claß holds that race, not religion or culture, is the root of difference and that Jews cannot be remade into Germans, so assimilation is not the aim; exclusion is.

elite-replacement.rationale: Claß believes Jews secretly mediate and manipulate; the later replacement conspiracy is an extension of that thinking, but not documented.

proportional-representation.rationale: Claß rejects the equal mass vote; proportional seats are a further democratic mechanism.

national-mission.rationale: The movement is particularist; it did not seek to export a form of government.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: No opened source discusses it; the movement's traditionalism and essentialism imply it would deny that society systematically favours men.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Claß says the court, the government and the conservatives have been blind to the Jewish enemy and that rulers are cut off from the people by a Jewish go-between.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: The article says Eugen Fischer's 1933 address used völkisch terms and that völkisch ideas shaped Nazi racial thinking.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Claß treats the state's force as essential and wants hardness against enemies.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Claß wants a state that expands abroad, curbs Social Democrats, restricts Jews and caps big banks, far beyond defence, justice and property.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The Wikipedia article on the League says it held Germans should be protected from mixing with other races, particularly Jews.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Claß says emancipation arose from the idea of human equality and calls that equality an untruth that will never be realised.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The statement belongs to Marxist theory of revolution; the movement opposed socialism outright and left no view on its internal debates.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Claß wants German settlement land and does not see settlement as illegitimate.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Inferred from Claß's wish for one nation under one law with special restrictions on Jews, not religious law.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Claß says religion is only an outflow of race, so conversion matters little; no demand is documented.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not addressed in any opened source; religious slaughter debates arose later, so no position is documented.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Inferred from the wish to Germanize Christianity and teach national spirituality in schools.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: This is an internal doctrine of Soviet-style socialism; the movement rejected socialism and did not weigh in on it.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Claß rejects the mass vote as untrue and unjust, grounding authority in nation, monarchy and merit.

trade-surplus.rationale: Claß wants industrial markets and raw material independence, favouring export strength.

population-transfer.rationale: The Wikipedia article on the League says it called for expelling Poles from Prussia and Claß called for depopulating Slav lands for German settlers.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Claß states army and fleet are also weapons of attack and wants an aggressive foreign policy.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Social Darwinism was strong in the League, though Chamberlain rejected it; the movement mainly sees peoples as competing.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Claß wants Bismarck's Socialist Law revived and all socialist leaders and editors expelled.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's authoritarian preferences make it unlikely to accept republican freedom.

separated-powers.rationale: Claß favoured a plebiscitary dictatorship and a stronger executive over checks.

vanguard-party.rationale: A Leninist doctrine opposed by Claß; the movement itself trusts the Volk's instinct.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Claß's priority is the nation, the Mittelstand and the educated and propertied, not the needy as a class; the Volk comes first, so mild disagreement.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Inferred from the movement's concern for small property and the Mittelstand that wider home ownership by ordinary Germans would be welcomed.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Claß complains employers face arbitrary action from Socialist workers without state protection.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Claß sees population growth as a source of national strength needing land, not as the cause of poverty.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Claß holds German and Jew are fire and water in essence and that shared national sentiment is needed for the state.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Claß says the worthy and capable should not be treated like the unfit; random selection of officials is the extreme of that equality.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Claß wants expulsions and hard action against Social Democrats and says there should be no sentimentality.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Claß complains of the wage-price spiral but proposes no price fixing; the sources give no basis for an answer.

party-controls-media.rationale: Claß wants socialist editors expelled and the press tamed, a step toward controlled media.

party-commands-army.rationale: The army belongs to the monarch or national state in the movement's tradition.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Claß wants resident Jews placed under restricted rights and the Volk defined by race.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Claß wants property and education represented; pay parity with workers is a Socialist idea.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Völkisch groups were fractious and anti-party in rhetoric, while leader-led dictatorship favours discipline; no stated view.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The Reich's sovereign will to power and rejection of internationalism rule out pooling.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Claß calls monarchy foundational and wants a strong crown, despite criticism of the court.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Adherents wanted a Germanized or pagan national faith; bishops not discussed.

clerical-rule.rationale: The movement exalted the Volk essence and rejected both Church authority and religious rulers.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Claß treats the masses' defection from the fatherland as the central danger; working for one's own government's defeat is the reverse of loyalty to the nation.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Inferred from the movement's campaign against decadence and for cultural rebirth that art harming national spirit would be censored.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Inferred from the movement's preference for a lasting strong leader or dictator over frequent mass elections.

recall-officials.rationale: Claß distrusts the mass electorate's power over rulers, so letting voters remove officials is disliked.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Claß wants an eternal alliance with Austria-Hungary for complete solidarity of interests.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: No source documents it; the movement liked property and small owners but a legal ban on renting is a radical measure not inferred from its programme.

people-in-arms.rationale: The League backed militarism and conscription but a citizen militia instead of professional army is not documented.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The Wikipedia article says the movement opposed urbanization and idealized rural life as authentic.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Claß wants an eternal bond with Austria and German leadership over Germans in Habsburg lands.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Claß presents the educated and propertied as the very group wrongly stripped of political voice, so he would reject calling them out of touch.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The Wikipedia article on Chamberlain's Foundations states he held Aryans preeminent among peoples and Teutons at the top.

death-penalty.rationale: Inferred from Claß's demand for hardness and no sentimentality toward the nation's enemies.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from the traditionalism and anti-modernism of the movement that liberal sex education and gender equality teaching would be opposed.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Völkisch thought used racial science and Darwinian ideas; creationism not a theme.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Inferred from the moral rebirth and anti-decadence outlook of the movement.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Claß says race is the source of danger and wants resident Jews' rights restricted; the nation is defined by descent.

minority-language-support.rationale: The League's central cause was agitation against Poles, including expulsions and expropriation, so state support for minority languages is rejected.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Claß demands uniform loyalty to the Volk and curbs on Jews, so special legal accommodation for minorities is unwelcome.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Claß praises German self-will as a trait but also demands submission to the national whole, so adherents are pulled both ways.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Not documented; inferred from the nation-first view that German finance gains no duty toward the world's poor, though cancelling debts owed to Germany is untested.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The statement concerns postcolonial states; the movement was itself colonial and offered no view.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Claß rejects mass electorates as the source of political authority, so a democratically elected assembly writing the constitution is disliked.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Claß would put national power above freedoms and urged limits on socialists and Jews, so temporary restriction is inferred as acceptable.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Claß's nation-first stance, with land and interest of the German people paramount, leaves no duty to the world's poor.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the demand that Germany become a power that does not rely on others.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Claß backed a plebiscitary dictatorship, which implies popular acclamation of a leader rather than parliamentary choice.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Not addressed in opened sources; the movement's stance on monetary institutions is undocumented.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: The League opposed the 1890 treaty giving up African holdings and demanded expansion.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Inferred from the organic Volk concept, where individual property serves the whole.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: An internal Marxist debate; the movement had no position.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Not addressed; nature romanticism suggests sympathy, industrial nationalism opposes it.

collective-defense.rationale: Claß wants an eternal alliance with Austria-Hungary and total solidarity of interests.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The movement demanded annexation of territory and denies other nations' feelings matter.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Mixed: Germanizing Christianity implied curbing churches, but not documented.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The League posed above party politics and Claß wants a strong crown, so a head of state above parties is congenial.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The League demands unconditional submission to the whole and favours imperial expansion, so force against secession is inferred as acceptable.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Claß wants unified national policy and German dominance in federal states like Austria-Hungary, so wide regional autonomy is disfavoured.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The movement valued a leader but not divine descent; pagan strands might differ.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The sources do not address income tax structure; no position can be inferred.

character-from-environment.rationale: Chamberlain's racialism and the Volk-essence concept treat gifts and character as innate to race, not formed by upbringing.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: A völkisch dictatorship answering to the Volk's will rather than to written law implies a ruler not bound by earlier legislation.

space-expansion.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement wanted land on earth and the sources give no view on space.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Not addressed; Claß wanted a stronger crown plus a franchise favouring the propertied, which hints at a mix, but this is not explicit.

leader-cult.rationale: The DVFP called for a völkisch dictatorship, implying a leader embodying the nation.

equal-parenting.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's family views are only inferred.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: An internal Marxist-Leninist debate; the movement had no position.

land-redistribution.rationale: Claß says that large estates can be broken into smaller farms, and the movement idealised peasants, so mild support is inferred.

refugee-return.rationale: Inferred from the concern for Germans abroad and homeland claims that expelled peoples should have a right to return.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Pan-Germanism, the League's core claim, was the demand that Germans be united in one state beyond borders.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Claß says religion is merely an outflow of race, so punishing religious change is not a völkisch aim.

women-must-cover.rationale: Alien to the movement's culture; no source suggests covering requirements.

common-currency.rationale: Claß's rejection of internationalism and love of national independence suggests opposition to sharing currency with other states.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The Wikipedia article describes the movement as Pan-German, aiming at union of German-descended peoples.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: League policy toward Poles denied them any self-governing schools or institutions; expropriation and expulsion were demanded instead.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Claß holds that Jews can never be Germans, so a minority's struggle for equal rights in Germany is rejected.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Claß says the teachers of materialism are Jews and that race is the source of the danger.

ban-cartels.rationale: Claß wants big-bank capital limited and shops suppressed to protect the Mittelstand; breaking up concentrated economic power is inferred, though he defends productive giants.

no-bailouts.rationale: Not addressed; Claß was ambivalent about big capital but gave no view on rescues.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Völkisch will of the Volk beats liberal constraints but majority democracy itself rejected.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred from the movement's traditionalism and from its rejection of equality that quotas for women would be opposed.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Claß wants colonies to supply raw materials and tropical products and end German dependence on others.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Binding international standards would limit national sovereignty, which the movement rejects.

moral-incentives.rationale: Claß praises the German who acts from honour rather than gain, so moral motives over material ones are favoured.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Claß conspired in coups and the DVFP demanded dictatorship, so small determined groups making change was accepted.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Langbehn favoured aristocracy and wanted a monarch, and the movement revered hereditary order.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The movement's national rebirth relied on teaching Germanic tradition and the Volk's past as the centre of education.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Claß claims colonies as settlement land and the Aryan superiority theory implies rule over others.

patriotic-education.rationale: National rebirth requires inculcating loyalty to the Volk; Claß's complaint is that the masses have lost love of fatherland.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred that adherents would reject any measure favouring minority groups, though their own policy discriminated by race.

public-money-creation.rationale: Not addressed; völkisch hostility to finance exists but no opened source states a monetary programme.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Not addressed; Claß says free play of forces hurts the Mittelstand but not that capitalism would collapse.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Claß wants a permanent bond with Austria-Hungary and German leadership there, and the movement idealised the Holy Roman Empire.

delink-world-market.rationale: The statement concerns postcolonial economies; the movement itself wanted colonies and did not address it.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist theory; the movement left no position on it.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Claß wanted discrimination imposed by the state, not private freedom, so the statement cuts both ways.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Rights of individuals are subordinate to the nation, so an entrenched bill limiting government is disliked.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Not addressed; the movement opposed ceding colonies but offered no view on treaties dividing peoples.

elective-rulers.rationale: Langbehn wanted a monarch and Claß treats monarchy as a foundation, so hereditary rule is preferred to elected rulers.

minority-veto.rationale: The League demands submission of individuals to the national whole, so a dissenting individual cannot hold up decisions.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Claß attacks the court as blind but remains monarchist; adherents split on removing rulers.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Claß wants parliamentary level raised by franchise reform but plans a plebiscitary dictatorship.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Inferred from nature romanticism; no opened source documents it.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred from nature romanticism and agrarian life that animal use with limited suffering is accepted.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Langbehn's aristocratic ideal, and the movement's picture of the organic Volk, imply the elite owes duties to the rest.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Claß and the League demanded active national politics from all patriots and condemn political apathy.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: The movement opposed mass society and rationalism and idealised an authentic rural Volk culture.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian thesis; the movement did not discuss it.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: A dependency theory the movement did not address.

native-born-offices.rationale: Claß wants the rights of resident Jews restricted, which includes exclusion from public office.

party-own-road.rationale: A communist-movement question; the movement had no position.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Claß wants colonies so Germany does not depend on others, and independence is a persistent nationalist theme.

return-lost-territory.rationale: The League opposed ceding African holdings in 1890 and Claß demanded annexations; revanchism was typical of its Weimar stance.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The movement favours rule by its own Volk and treats settlement of conquered land as legitimate.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Anachronistic; a movement that demanded dictatorship would reject it as a constitutional value.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Not documented; the movement attacked communism but would not accept equivalence with its own dictatorial leanings.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not addressed; American history is outside the sources.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from the movement's reverence for national tradition and heroes.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's gender views are only inferred.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not addressed in any source opened.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Claß says the equal vote works only when voters share a national and state spirit, so liberal institutions suit only some peoples.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Claß planned coups with army backing and wanted the army as an instrument of the nation's power.

paid-care-work.rationale: Not addressed; traditionalism points one way, Volk pronatalism another.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred from the movement's traditionalism and organic community.

office-by-exam.rationale: Not addressed; merit is praised but via aristocracy and leaders, not examinations.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Claß wants state protection of national enterprise and of land from foreign hands; inferred approval of blocking foreign purchases of strategic firms.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from traditionalism that easy divorce would be disliked.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Claß rejects mass control of rulers, so delegates bound by and removable by voters is the opposite of his plan.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Blood and soil thinking ties land to the Volk but peasants held hereditary property; no clear answer.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Claß wants parliament reformed but not abolished, and the sources are silent on budget powers.

single-official-language.rationale: League policy against Poles aimed at German as the one language of public life.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Claß proposes expropriation and a ban on parcelling land aimed at Poles in the east.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred from the movement's belief in innate racial differences that unequal outcomes are not proof of discrimination.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Claß blames materialism and the pursuit of gain, contrasted with German honour, for national decline.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Not addressed; no source discusses covert foreign policy.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Claß wants German leadership in Austria-Hungary but says nothing on troops entering allied states.

corporate-influence.rationale: Claß says big capital endangers the Mittelstand and a Jewish mediator controls government access, so overweening private influence is criticised.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from nationalist suspicion of foreign and Jewish influence.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Claß treats rapid German population growth as strength and a justification for land.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred from the anti-foreign land stance and from hostility to outsiders.

job-guarantee.rationale: Not addressed in any opened source.

democratic-peace.rationale: The movement rejected democracy and war-averse liberalism, and the claim is not part of its worldview.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The League demands unconditional submission of individuals to the state and nation.

non-intervention.rationale: Claß urges an aggressive foreign policy that ignores other states' wishes.

industrial-unions.rationale: Claß opposes socialist unions entirely; the organisational form is not discussed.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Claß states Jews stand between government and people and lead the Socialists in poisoning the voters.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Marriage and family were seen as the base of the Volk's reproduction; abolition is the reverse.

local-production.rationale: Inferred from the agrarian, rooted, anti-urban ideal.

informal-organisation.rationale: The movement favoured leader-led parties and leagues; anarchist informal groups are alien.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Claß rejects internationalism and puts the state's will to power first.

religious-nation.rationale: Claß says religion only plays a role as an outflow of race, so the nation is defined by blood, not faith.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Claß wants German dominion and refuses to defer to others.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Claß wants a unified Reich with national, not regional, priorities.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Claß defends property generally, so the idea of holding the means of production in common is rejected.

defeat-communism.rationale: Claß says the Social Democrat leadership must be removed and the fight pursued without half measures.

religion-illusion.rationale: The movement's spiritual romanticism and its materialism critique reject treating religion as illusion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Claß criticises free play of forces and materialism; this Marxist praise of capitalism is not his view.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from the movement's traditionalism; the premise is Marxist.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred from the movement's emphasis on the traditional family as the base.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Inferred from the cultural-purity concerns of the movement and of Claß's Deutschbund, which promoted pure Germanism.

treaties-binding.rationale: Claß rejects constraint on the national will to land, so treaties with minorities would not be binding.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Inferred from the agrarian ideal of rooted rural communities.

majority-settlement.rationale: Claß and the League sought German settlers in conquered eastern lands and expropriation of Poles.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Claß attacks both socialist agitation and the free play of forces, which matches a third course.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The League and Claß justified eastern expansion by German need and by earlier German settlement and rule.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Anachronistic: the movement ended in 1945 and its pre-1945 adherents could not answer; post-war remnants split.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred from the traditionalism of the movement and the laws of its time.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Claß demands expulsion of all Social Democrat officials and editors and a revived Socialist Law.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Adherents split between Christians and pagans; no source suggests blasphemy laws.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Claß seeks colonies for industrial markets, raw materials and German settlement.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: An Islamic doctrine the movement did not address.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's religion was folk-based rather than ruled by religious law.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Claß rejects the mass vote and treats the masses as misled, so broad popular decision-making is rejected.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The statement presupposes equality; Claß rejects human equality and race-blind analysis.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the movement's traditionalism.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed; racial hygiene inclinations and traditionalism pull opposite ways.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Inferred from the movement's claim to unite nation and renew beyond liberal and socialist parties.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxist concept; romantic anti-industrial thought shares the concern but the movement did not frame it so.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Inferred from the movement's ethnic and cultural exclusivism; Islam is not discussed in the sources.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Adherents split between a Germanized Christianity and revived Germanic paganism, and authority was grounded in the Volk and a leader rather than clearly in God.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: The sources do not address religious dress; inferred that a Volk state favoured visible national and Christian-cultural identity over a neutral public sphere.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: No source addresses harassment or contracts; inferred from the movement's authoritarian, anti-liberal and patriarchal outlook that it had no interest in individual rights claims against employers.

social-market-economy.rationale: Claß defends property and the Mittelstand and the movement idealised agrarian life, but it prescribed no market-plus-welfare model and adherents differed; inferred.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Claß and the Pan-German League demanded expansion, conquest and a strong military as the means of national survival.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred from the organic-Volk idea that the national body's members share fate; the sources do not address staged development, though the Mittelstand was favoured over a rich elite.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Pan-Germans pursued aggressive expansion and great-power alliances and rejected restraint abroad, so neutrality contradicted their programme.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Langbehn's programme favoured aristocratic, monarchist leadership, though Claß wanted a plebiscitary dictator; inheritance within a family is inferred as acceptable.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Völkisch writers attacked finance capital, but no source discusses user-owned credit; adherents' view is unknown.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred from the movement's hostility to foreign influence and insistence on national sovereignty; the issue is anachronistic.

property-franchise.rationale: Claß's programme rejected equal suffrage and wanted the vote weighted toward the propertied and the Volk's established stock.

domination-women-nature.rationale: The movement idealised nature and rural life but held a patriarchal view of women; it never framed the two as one logic of domination.

reification.rationale: Völkisch thinkers rejected Marxist analysis and treated market and class relations as secondary to race and nation; inferred.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Antisemites attacked a supposedly Jewish-controlled press, but they did not make the leftist claim about wealth emptying formal freedoms.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The movement sought an authoritarian state ruled by a leader and the Volk's will, rejecting liberal legal constraints on rulers.

racial-franchise.rationale: Racial belonging was the core of the programme and Claß demanded Jews be stripped of political rights.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the movement's rejection of democracy and parliamentary deliberation.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from its authoritarian, leader-centred politics, which rejected public scrutiny of rulers.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Race-mixing with Jews was condemned and bans on such marriages were demanded, though on racial rather than religious grounds.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Antisemitic boycotts of Jewish businesses were a staple of völkisch agitation, though justified by race.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of democracy and preference for leadership by the racially chosen and the strong.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Völkisch writers like Chamberlain recast Christianity in Germanic terms, rejecting its Jewish roots, though some went to neopaganism; adherents were split.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The sources do not discuss wealth concentration and liberty; it opposed liberal capitalism but also liberal equality, so adherents' view is unclear.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from its cult of martial national virtue and its rejection of liberal equality and modern degeneracy.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Inferred from its ideal of a national religion rooted in Germanic or Germanized Christian tradition, which is hostile to state-promoted unbelief and rationalism.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred from its demand for a strong authoritarian state and order; it never contemplated abolishing police or prisons.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Its organic, racially defined Volk and rejection of liberal equality and parliamentarism are incompatible with guaranteed shares for communities.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Not documented; the organic Volk idea implies mutual care among Germans but the sources are silent on charity versus state aid.

term-limits.rationale: Not documented; it rejected parliamentary democracy so elected office limits were not a live issue.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of parliamentary democracy and liberal equality in favour of authoritarian leadership.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of rationalism and modernity and its focus on national rebirth and expansion rather than humanity's long-term survival.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from its idealisation of traditional, rural roles and a national (Christian or pagan) religion led by men.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from its idealisation of traditional rural life and patriarchal family order.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Claß wanted residents outside the German Volk, above all Jews, stripped of civil and political rights, so voting for foreigners is rejected.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from its stress on a strong state serving the Volk and its dislike of liberal economics; housing policy is not discussed.

abolish-ip.rationale: The sources do not address it; inferred from the nationalist and Romantic cult of national genius, which favours protecting creators' works.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred from the movement's cult of youth, rural renewal and hardening, seen in the Wandervogel-style milieu; the sources do not name drilled national-service groups.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Nuclear weapons postdate the movement; its militarism would favour them but its sovereignty stress is silent on basing.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from the Pan-German League's demand for full German sovereignty and rejection of foreign influence; bases are anachronistic.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred from its ethnic-supremacist outlook, which would not want the Volk's wrongs or other peoples' victimhood made a state matter; anachronistic.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Its anticapitalist, anti-urban strand, including Langbehn, favoured labour and the soil over finance, but no programme is documented.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Claß demands war and conquest, and the movement glorified martial struggle, so a ban on lethal force is rejected.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The article describes the Volk as an organic body with a quasi-eternal essence, which is exactly an unbroken line from ancient origins.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: The movement grounded identity and sex roles in organic and biological essence, so constructionism is the opposite of its view.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred from its organic, hierarchical view of society with fixed roles for women; feminism is not a concern of the sources.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from its cult of sacrifice for the Volk; the sources do not document a martyr cult directly.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Chamberlain's Foundations casts history as a racial struggle with spiritual stakes, but sources do not frame all politics as good against evil.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The Pan-German League wanted to gather Germans abroad into the Reich and settle conquered land, which opposes a diaspora-centre model.

culture-before-state.rationale: Langbehn and the wider movement sought national rebirth on reconstructed Germanic culture, though the League also wanted a strong state at once.

god-not-male.rationale: Adherents split between Germanized Christianity and a revived Germanic paganism, and both pictured a male, patriarchal God.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred from its patriarchal and anti-liberal outlook; it did not judge traditions by women's standing.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Claß wanted Germans to dominate the nation's life and Jews pushed out of the economy and public life, stated forcefully.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: The League sought unification of Germans across borders, which favours merging German-settled regions, though not framed in these terms.

independent-unions.rationale: Claß's programme was authoritarian and anti-socialist, so independent unions are inferred as unwelcome.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The movement demanded the expulsion of socialist agitators and a strong state, so workers' own political power was no part of its idea of the nation.

local-essentials-public.rationale: The sources do not discuss public utilities; the movement's economic views are sparse.

second-chamber.rationale: Langbehn wanted a monarchy and aristocratic leadership but the sources describe no particular chamber structure.

municipal-property.rationale: Claß defended property and the Mittelstand, so community ownership of production is inferred as rejected.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The Pan-German League wanted a strong, centralized state and opposed democratization, so binding power resting with local assemblies is inferred as foreign.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred from the movement's idealization of rural family life and the Volk as an organic body.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Anachronistic; no source bears on drug regulation.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Inferred from the movement's rejection of modern rationalism and its natural-order view of life.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the demand for a strong authoritarian state that surveils and controls.

online-anonymity.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the League's insistence on submission to the national whole and state authority.

person-over-state.rationale: The League demanded submission of the individual to the national whole, so the person was subordinate to the Volk.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The movement rejected rationalism and materialism and sought national rebirth through myth, tradition and a Germanic spiritual essence.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred from the League's centralizing nationalism and opposition to autonomy within the Reich.

gm-crops.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the rejection of industrial modernity and reverence for natural, rural life.

dense-cities.rationale: Langbehn wanted Germany to abandon urbanization for an agrarian society, so cities were disfavored, though not for environmental reasons.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Claß treats race as the basis of political life and demands that Germans organize to defend themselves against what he calls racial danger.

racial-pride.rationale: Chamberlain's racial theory asserts Aryan and Teutonic pre-eminence, and pride in German blood was central.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Claß and the League demanded annexation of land and aggressive war aims, so force was for pursuing national aims, not only defense.

missingStatements.text: The nation's identity should be rooted in a revived pre-Christian ancestral religion rather than in the Christian churches.
missingStatements.rationale: The common core of the movement was national rebirth on reconstructed Germanic traditions, with adherents wanting either a Germanized Christianity or a revived Germanic paganism (the pagan wing answers +2, the Christian wing -1).
missingStatements.declined: A single strand of one movement; no other ideology would take a position on a revived pre-Christian national religion, and national-rebirth covers the theme.

missingStatements.text: Members of a particular ethnic minority should have fewer civil and political rights than the majority.
missingStatements.rationale: Claß writes that the rights of the resident Jewish population must be generally restricted, even when the good suffer with the bad, because race is the source of the danger.

missingStatements.text: A nation's land and its people are bound together, and its peasantry is the source of its strength.
missingStatements.rationale: The article names blood and soil and agrarianism among the movement's concepts, and Langbehn wanted Germany to abandon industrialization and urbanization for an agrarian society.

notes: The movement was not unified: Chamberlain rejected social Darwinism while the Pan-German League embraced it, Langbehn favoured peace while Claß urged aggressive war, and adherents split between Christian and pagan wings. Many economic, gender and technology answers are inferred (low confidence). Statements about the Holocaust and post-1945 issues are anachronistic for the historical movement.
